newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end sharply higher as funds buy.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end sharply higher as funds buy.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed sharply up with contract highs established in the first three positions, boosted by fund buying and growing sentiment that cash prices look set to advance.
"We had a lot of fund buying and I think people are looking for at least $65 (per cwt) in the cash market next week," one dealer said.

Dealers noted heavy cash movement Wednesday eased concern about feedlots getting behind with marketings. USDA reported 72,000 head traded in Texas/west Oklahoma at a steady $64 per cwt, and 65,100 head traded in Kansas.

Floor sources said Prudential Securities and R.J. O'Brien were featured late buyers of August while ING and R.J. O'Brien were buyers of October. August selling was scattered while Cargill Investor Services were an October seller.
Aug, Oct and Dec set contract highs, with August topping at 67.475 cents a lb and closing up 0.725 cent at 67.425 cents. Other months were up 0.850 to down 0.200 cent.

Feeder cattle futures also closed higher, boosted partly by weakness in CBOT corn prices. August feeders closed up 0.175 cent at 82.850 cents a lb with other months showing gains of 0.450 to 0.200 cent.

Floor sources noted Cargill Investor Services bought October and sold August all day while Iowa Grain and ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp were late sellers of August. Smith Barney was a featured buyer of August.
"The feeling is that input costs are going down," said Don Roose, president of U.S. Commodities.
The latest CME feeder cattle index, for July 23, was up $0.18 at $82.17, its highest level since March 17, 1994.
CBOT September corn futures closed on Thursday down 3-3/4 cents at $2.43-1/2 a bushel, sharply below a year ago with corn prices setting a record high of $5.54-1/2 in July 1996.
